references.text: The same principle that an animal vowed to the Lord must not be exchanged, and if it is exchanged, both the original and the replacement shall be holy.
The preceding verse explaining the context of the tithe of cattle and sheep passing under the shepherd's staff.
Ezekiel uses similar language about separating animals, where the Lord will judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and goats.
The principle that certain holy things cannot be redeemed or exchanged.
A similar provision that something devoted to the Lord as banished property cannot be sold or redeemed.
